questions.q: What should you always start with when designing a service?
options: Learning about the people who will use it
questions.explain: If you don't understand who users are and what they need, you can't build the right thing.
questions.evidence: When designing a government service, always start by learning about the people who will use it.

questions.q: When should you plan user research?
options: At the start of each development phase, updating the plan as you learn
questions.explain: Research objectives change as the team learns more in each phase.
questions.evidence: You should plan user research at the start of each development phase, and regularly update your plan as you learn more about your users.

options: Visiting people in their everyday environment to observe how they do an activity
Testing a prototype in a lab
questions.explain: Seeing people use their own equipment, with their usual distractions, reveals real needs.
questions.evidence: Contextual research means visiting people in their everyday environment (like their home, work or school) to observe how they do an activity.

questions.q: What is a risk of the 'five whys' method?
options: Repeatedly asking why can make interviewees feel frustrated or defensive
questions.explain: Use it carefully and make sure people feel heard.
questions.evidence: Sometimes asking why multiple times can cause the interviewee to feel frustrated or defensive if they don’t feel as if they are being heard.

questions.q: When should a team analyse a research session?
options: As soon as possible after each round, while it is still fresh
At the end of the project
questions.explain: Analysing together also helps the team agree what to work on next.
questions.evidence: You should do analysis as soon as you can after each round of research, while it is still fresh in people’s minds.

questions.q: Why shouldn't placeholder personas made without research drive design decisions?
options: They take too long to write
questions.explain: Personas must come from research to represent real users.
questions.evidence: because they're effectively stereotypes, avoid using them for implementable design decisions.

questions.q: What does an experience map show?
options: What users do, think and feel over time, from first needing a service to when they stop using it
A list of features ranked by cost
questions.explain: It covers the whole journey, including events and related services outside your own.
questions.evidence: Experience maps provide a visual representation of what users do, think and feel over time, from the point they start needing a service to when they stop using it.

questions.q: Why are code prototypes better for user research than paper sketches?
options: They can be used in production
questions.explain: You must prototype and test designs before committing to build anything.
questions.evidence: Code prototypes are better for user research because they’re more realistic.

questions.q: What should headings in a user interface do?
options: Repeat the first sentence of the text
Describe the purpose of the text that follows, without being part of it
questions.explain: Clear headings help people scan and find what they need.
questions.evidence: Headings should describe the purpose of the text that follows - they should not be part of the text.

questions.q: In moderated usability testing, why ask participants to 'think aloud'?
options: It helps you understand what they are doing, thinking and feeling
It is required for recording consent
questions.explain: Hearing their reasoning shows why they struggle, not just where.
questions.evidence: Asking them to ‘think aloud’ as they move through the service helps you understand what they are doing, thinking and feeling.

questions.q: How is accessibility different from assisted digital support?
options: Assisted digital support means helping people use the online parts of a service
Accessibility only applies to printed letters
Assisted digital support is only for blind users
questions.explain: Accessibility means the service itself can be used by as many people as possible.
questions.evidence: Accessibility is different from assisted digital support , which means helping people to use the online parts of your service.
